Recognition of deferred tax asset in the consolidated and separate financial statements
See Note 2(ii)(c), 3, and 15 to the consolidated and separate (cid:285)nancial statements

column2: How the key audit matter was addressed in our audit

column1:
The Group and Company has recognised deferred tax
assets of KShs 185 million and KShs 161 million respectively
for deductible temporary differences and unused tax
losses that it believes are recoverable.
The recoverability of recognised deferred tax assets is
in part dependent on the Group’s and Company’s ability
to generate future taxable pro(cid:285)ts suf(cid:285)cient to utilise
deductible temporary differences and tax losses.
We have determined recognition of deferred tax assets to
be a key audit matter because of the inherent uncertainty in
forecasting the amount and timing of future taxable pro(cid:285)ts
and the reversal of temporary differences, especially in the
light of the recent history of losses.
column2:
Our audit procedures in this area included:
• Using our own tax specialist to evaluate the accuracy
of tax computations and temporary differences
upon which the Group and Company has recognized
deferred tax assets.
• Assessing the reasonableness of forecast future
taxable pro(cid:285)ts by comparing the forecast taxable
pro(cid:285)ts to our own understanding of the business plans
used to support the going concern assumptions and
to projected revenue based on sales orders relating
to the subsequent year received at the reporting
date.
• Evaluating the adequacy of the consolidated and
separate (cid:285)nancial statements disclosures, including
disclosures of key assumptions and judgements.
